 <item> <title>Ukraine: the environment as a target (I)</title>
 <link>https://news.cnrs.fr/articles/ukraine-the-environment-as-a-target-i</link>
 <description>Ukrainian researchers are documenting the destruction of their environment in real time, with the aim of estimating what can be restored and how, and how long it will take. </description>

 <item> <title>When the living aims high</title>
 <link>https://news.cnrs.fr/articles/when-the-living-aims-high</link>
 <description>Humans aren't the only ones who may be forced to migrate due to climate change. A host of other species are also leaving their original homes and settling in habitats with a cooler climate, bringing the risk of increased competition with one another. </description>

 <item> <title>Turning waste into wealth</title>
 <link>https://news.cnrs.fr/articles/turning-waste-into-wealth</link>
 <description>Researchers and manufacturers are exploring ways of capturing CO2, storing it, or even turning it into a resource. The challenge now is to develop the infrastructure needed to move up from research to large-scale industrial applications. </description>
 <category>Matter, Earth</category>

 <item> <title>War and peace</title>
 <link>https://news.cnrs.fr/articles/war-and-peace</link>
 <description>Whilst war fractures societies, it can bring about reinforced bonds within the communities it targets. By analysing ethnic conflicts across 36 African countries, an economist reveals the mechanisms that forge identities and strengthen cohesion.</description>
 <category>Society</category>
 <enclosure url="https://news.cnrs.fr/sites/default/files/styles/social/public/assets/images/1_rea6396310_vp.jpg?itok=xxGnyaV5" length="173731" type="image/jpeg" />

</item>
 <item> <title>Death, a down-to-earth matter</title>
 <link>https://news.cnrs.fr/articles/death-a-down-to-earth-matter</link>
 <description>What should be done with our bodies once we die? Should they be burned, buried, or just allowed to decompose naturally? A group of researchers from the CNRS is exploring this third, environmentally friendly option – including in the afterlife, which has been dubbed “terramation”. </description>
 <category>Life, Society</category>
 <enclosure url="https://news.cnrs.fr/sites/default/files/styles/social/public/assets/images/1_hemis_4248382_vp.jpg?itok=RbEkgLMZ" length="350153" type="image/jpeg" />

</item>
 <item> <title>Searching the Milky Way for bits of Mars</title>
 <link>https://news.cnrs.fr/articles/searching-the-milky-way-for-bits-of-mars</link>
 <description>The MMX mission successfully launched on 19 October, heading for Phobos, one of Mars's moons. The aim is to deploy the Idefix mini-rover on the surface, and for the very first time return samples from the Mars system to Earth.</description>

 <item> <title>Surrogacy in keeping with Chinese tradition</title>
 <link>https://news.cnrs.fr/articles/surrogacy-in-keeping-with-chinese-tradition</link>
 <description>Surrogacy is on the rise in China, even though it is officially banned. The anthropologist Renyou Hou examines how the technique could alter family relationships while fitting in with traditional practices.</description>

 <item> <title>Cancer resistance yields fundamental secret</title>
 <link>https://news.cnrs.fr/articles/cancer-resistance-yields-fundamental-secret</link>
 <description>As breast cancer awareness month is unfolding, and with World Day Against Breast Cancer being held on October 19, research on one of its most aggressive forms, triple-negative breast cancer, is advancing. Studies by a team at Institut Curie, in Paris, have now highlighted a hitherto unknown behaviour of cancer cells in response to treatments. </description>
 <category>Life</category>
 <enclosure url="https://news.cnrs.fr/sites/default/files/styles/social/public/assets/images/1_cnrs_20220073_0017_vp.jpg?itok=LT9Ovbek" length="114909" type="image/jpeg" />

 <item> <title>Long-forgotten women's health</title>
 <link>https://news.cnrs.fr/articles/long-forgotten-womens-health</link>
 <description>Designated as Women's Health Month internationally, October is dotted with dedicated awareness campaigns and events. Yet health is another area in which women are victims of gender inequalities. Although research is finally taking an interest in the female body’s specific reactions to disease, clinical trials are only now beginning to include more women.</description>
 <category>Life, Society</category>
